title: Pushes and pulls in play
keyIdea: A push moves a thing away from you and a pull brings it towards you. Pushes and pulls are forces: they make things start to move, go faster, change direction or stop. A bigger push makes a toy car go further and a swing go higher; a gentle push only moves it a little. A thing moves away from the side you push it from. You pull a drawer to open it and push it to shut it.

kid: Kick a ball and it goes away from you. That is a push. Tug a rope and it comes to you. That is a pull.
Give a toy car a little push. It rolls a little way. Give it a big push. Off it goes, a long way! A big push makes it go further.
Push a ball from this side, and it rolls the other way. It goes away from your hand. So stand on the side away from the goal.
To open a drawer, pull the handle to you. To shut it, push it in. A swing goes up high when you give it big pushes.
adult: This is early physics. Development Matters asks three and four year olds to explore how things work and to talk about the forces they feel, such as a push or a pull. In Year 3 children learn that a force is a push or a pull, and later that forces can change the speed, direction and shape of objects. The aim now is the words push, pull, harder, gentle, faster, further and direction, linked to things a child has done.

The science under the play: a push acts away from the person and a pull acts towards them. A larger force on the same toy gives it more speed, so it rolls further before friction stops it. A ball moves off in the direction of the push, so you push from the side opposite where you want it to go. A swing goes higher when each push adds more energy.

Common mistakes: thinking a push brings things towards you; calling every action with the hands a push; expecting a gentle push to send a car as far as a strong one; pushing a ball from the goal side and expecting it to go in; pushing a drawer to open it. Ask them to say which way the thing moved: away from me, or towards me?

In the lab your child sorts actions such as kicking a ball and opening a drawer into push or pull, drags a hand back to give a car a gentle, middle or strong push and parks it in a spot, pushes a ball from the side that sends it into the goal, opens and shuts a drawer and a door, and pushes a swing up to a star.

familyTip: Play with a ball or a toy car on the floor. Ask: is that a push or a pull? Try a little push and a big push and mark where it stops with a sock. Which went further?

visual.caption: Push or pull? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: push a door that says PUSH
pull a wagon by its handle

lab.caption: Flagship lab: sort pushes and pulls, push a car, a ball and a swing, and open a drawer and a door.

practice.prompt: You pull a wagon. Which way does it go?
practice.hint: A pull brings things to you.
practice.explain: A pull brings the wagon towards you. A push would send it away.

practice.prompt: A gentle push rolls the car {n} steps. A strong push rolls it 2 steps more. How far does the strong push go?
practice.hint: Start at {n} and count on 2 more steps.
practice.explain: {n} and 2 more is {=n+2} steps. The strong push goes further.

practice.prompt: How do you open a drawer?
practice.hint: Does the drawer come towards you or go away?
practice.explain: The drawer comes out towards you, so you pull it. You push it to shut it.

practice.prompt: You give the swing {n} big pushes and then 1 more. How many pushes is that?

pool.prompt: You kick a ball. Is that a push or a pull?
choices: Not a push or a pull
pool.hint: Does the ball go away from you or come to you?
pool.explain: Your foot sends the ball away, so a kick is a push.

pool.prompt: Which push makes a toy car go the furthest?
pool.explain: A strong push makes the car go fastest, so it rolls the furthest.

pool.prompt: The goal is on your left. Where do you push the ball from?
pool.hint: A ball rolls away from the push.
pool.explain: Push from the right and the ball rolls left, away from your hand, into the goal.

pool.prompt: A door has a sign that says PUSH. How do you open it?
pool.hint: Read the sign. It tells you which way to move the door.
pool.explain: A PUSH door opens away from you, so you push it.

pool.prompt: The swing only goes up a little. What will make it go higher?
pool.hint: Think about big and gentle pushes.
pool.explain: A bigger push makes the swing go higher. A gentle one only moves it a little.

pool.prompt: You tug a rope towards you. Is that a push or a pull?
choices: Not a push or a pull
pool.hint: Which way does the rope move?
pool.explain: The rope comes towards you, so tugging is a pull.

pool.prompt: A gentle push rolls a ball {n} steps. A strong push rolls it twice as far. How many steps is that?
pool.hint: Twice as far means {n} and {n} again.

pool.prompt: You open {n} drawers. Each one needs 1 pull to open and 1 push to shut. How many pushes and pulls is that?
pool.hint: Count 2 for each drawer: a pull and a push.
pool.explain: Each drawer needs 2, so {n} drawers need {=2*n} pushes and pulls.
